central_node: Topographical Dynamics, Water Storage, and River Ecology

key_details: Rivers originate from melting glaciers, springs, or heavy rain
Fast water velocity cuts steep mountain valleys
Erodes rocks and transports coarse sediments
real_world_examples: River Godavari originating at Trimbakeshwar in Western Ghats

key_details: Water velocity slows down across flat plains
Water is diverted into irrigation canals for agriculture
Deposits fine silt near the sea to form river deltas
real_world_examples: Godavari river delta discharging into the Bay of Bengal

key_details: Dams block river flow to create large artificial reservoirs
Supplies drinking water during dry seasons
Provides irrigation for farming and generates hydroelectric power
real_world_examples: Over 900 large dams built across major Indian rivers

key_details: Reservoirs submerge upstream forest habitats
Displaces local human villages and wildlife
Alters natural river flow and sediment transport
real_world_examples: Community resettlement near dam reservoir sites

key_details: Ganges river dolphin lives in muddy freshwater rivers
It is blind due to turbid muddy water conditions
Uses ultrasonic sound waves (echolocation) to navigate and hunt
real_world_examples: Ganges river dolphin in the Ganga river basin

key_details: Cleaning polluted rivers by treating industrial effluents
Constructing sewage treatment plants along riverbanks
Encouraging public action to prevent waste dumping
real_world_examples: Namami Gange Programme along the river Ganga

key_details: Some rivers do not reach the open sea or ocean
Terminates in inland salt marshes and desert sinks
real_world_examples: Luni river terminating in the Rann of Kutch (Gujarat)
